- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 forecast values before final output.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment’s dominant trend over last 7 days.
